title: 3D Artist Master Skill Tree
generated_for: Career progression from Beginner to Art Director
note: This is a competency model, not a claim that every artist must master every tool. Specialization branches indicate where depth is expected.

must_be_able_to: Understand basic form, proportion, perspective, value and color.
Create simple clean 3D forms.
Use a primary DCC without constant tutorial dependence.
Read and analyze reference.

junior.focus: Create simple production-ready assets under guidance.
must_be_able_to: Model simple props and assets from reference.
Create UVs, bake maps and author basic PBR textures.
Follow project naming, folder and export conventions.
Integrate assets into an engine and perform basic self-QA.

junior_plus.focus: Own complete small assets and solve common technical/artistic issues.
must_be_able_to: Complete an asset from blockout through engine integration.
Diagnose common topology, UV, bake and material problems.
Use Unreal or another target engine productively.
Work with less supervision.

middle.focus: Independently deliver production assets and contribute to scenes.
must_be_able_to: Own complex assets or environment sections.
Make sound quality/performance tradeoffs.
Use procedural, material and engine systems when appropriate.
Collaborate effectively across disciplines.

middle_plus.focus: Handle complex ownership and ambiguous requirements.
must_be_able_to: Solve non-routine production problems.
Estimate work and identify dependencies.
Improve local workflows.
Maintain consistent quality across a larger body of work.

senior.focus: Independent expert execution, problem solving and technical/artistic leadership.
must_be_able_to: Own difficult assets, systems or environment sections end-to-end.
Diagnose root causes rather than patch symptoms.
Balance visual quality, performance, schedule and pipeline constraints.
Mentor artists and establish reliable workflows.
Set quality standards and workflows.
Coordinate artists across a feature or discipline.
Make high-impact technical and artistic tradeoffs.
Mentor, review, plan and unblock the team.

principal.focus: Cross-project technical/artistic influence and systems thinking.
must_be_able_to: Design scalable pipelines and reusable systems.
Solve organization-level production problems.
Define standards across teams.
Influence engine, tools and art direction decisions.

art_director.focus: Creative direction, visual strategy and organizational leadership.
must_be_able_to: Define and maintain a coherent visual identity.
Translate creative vision into production standards.
Lead multidisciplinary art teams.
Make portfolio, staffing, schedule and quality decisions.

mastery_scale.name: conceptual
mastery_scale.definition: Понимает принцип и может объяснить его.

mastery_scale.name: independent
mastery_scale.definition: Может выполнить самостоятельно на типовой задаче.

mastery_scale.definition: Может обучать и стандартизировать применение навыка.

mastery_scale.name: expert
mastery_scale.definition: Определяет best practices и влияет на направление.

validation_notes: Unreal Engine is treated as a first-class branch rather than a single skill.
The tree separates transferable fundamentals from tool-specific implementation.

Nanite, Lumen, PCG, Virtual Shadow Maps, Niagara, World Partition and modern material workflows are included because current Unreal documentation treats them as major rendering/world-building systems.
Senior+ is defined primarily by autonomy, problem solving, ownership, optimization, mentoring and system-level impact rather than years of experience.
Use the source URLs for version-specific Unreal details because engine capabilities and recommended workflows change over time.
